This is a Sprague-Grundy type problem, or more simply a P-position/N-position analysis.

A position N is a P-position (previous player wins, i.e., the player who just moved wins, meaning the current player loses) if all moves lead to N-positions.

A position N is an N-position (next player wins) if there exists a move leading to a P-position.

The allowed moves from N are: subtract 1, subtract any prime p, subtract any multiple of n (kn for k≥1).
